key_insight: DNS-calibrated profile transformations predict friction and heat transfer in water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity within 2% of DNS, except at the lowest Reynolds numbers.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for water-property variations can improve thermal-hydraulic predictions where constant-property assumptions substantially misestimate drag and heat transfer.
method: Run plane-channel DNS of heated and cooled water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity.
Derive integral profile transformations from mean momentum and energy balances, with DNS-calibrated turbulence corrections.
Apply the corrections to the Spalart–Allmaras model to improve friction predictions.
evidence_signal: Across wall temperatures of 277–360 K and wall Prandtl numbers of 2–12, friction changed by −39% to +32% relative to constant-property flow, while empirical correlations deviated from DNS by up to 26%.
watch_item: The corrections are calibrated on plane-channel DNS, and accuracy weakens at the lowest Reynolds numbers; transfer to other geometries requires validation.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent heat transfer in water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity
